draft.briefing: Hey, you're near the Edakkal Caves! Inside, people carved figures, animals and symbols into the rock at least six thousand years ago. It's a steep climb, but worth every step.
draft.hungryLine: Food around here is simple. Grab a meal in Ambalavayal before or after the climb.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Climb to Edakkal Caves early, then visit the Wayanad Heritage Museum in Ambalavayal.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit at the top of Ambukuthi Mala after the climb and look out over Wayanad.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The caves were rediscovered by a British police officer, Fred Fawcett, while he was out hunting in the 1890s.

status.text: Entry is capped each day, go early

spots.name: Phantom Rock
spots.detail: 10 min drive · A rock shaped like a skull

legends.title: A cave made by an arrow
legends.body: Edakkal means 'a stone in between'. A boulder fell into a crack in the hill and made the roof of the cave.

legends.title: The hill of the arrow
legends.body: Legend says Rama's sons shot an arrow into this hill, and that's how the cave began.

tips.title: Start the climb early.
tips.body: The path is steep, and the sun gets strong by noon.

tips.title: Wear good shoes.
tips.body: The last part of the climb is on rock and ladders.

story.title: Carvings in the rock
story.body: Neolithic people carved human figures, animals and symbols into the cave walls.

story.title: More carvings
story.body: Later visitors added inscriptions in old scripts, layer on top of layer.

story.title: Rediscovered
story.body: Fred Fawcett, a police officer in Malabar, found the caves and wrote about them.

story.title: Protecting the caves
story.body: To protect the carvings, the number of daily visitors is now limited.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Climb up, find the oldest carving you can, then rest at the top. Tell me which figure you liked.
